plan.G: No integrated candidate is available during preparation. After research, integrate only measured, correct candidates; remeasure the combined program because gains may not be additive, and independently confirm final G before selecting it by the official criterion.
plan.analysis: Choose N=3: the supplied run exposes three complementary opportunities without prescribing a fixed tree count. The baseline is correct and has three timing samples with a reported mean of 0.002672 s (score 0.5); the supplied record does not break those measurements down by size or thread budget. The source computes each element serially, performs log/sqrt/exp work and evaluates the CND approximation, while run ignores the supplied threads argument. Thus thread-level parallelism, lane-level math optimization, and scalar expression simplification merit separate measurements. Keep every candidate general for the public contract, write the entire output, respect the thread budget, and validate against the stated tolerance. Treat speedups as hypotheses until measured.

children.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, parallelize the independent element loop without changing Black–Scholes or CND arithmetic. Respect the caller's thread budget for every valid call and write all n outputs. Compare a direct serial path when threads is one with team creation, and test a race-free static partition for larger budgets; do not assume the only valid budgets are the timed ones. Check correctness and wall time at both supplied sizes and budgets, keeping a variant only if its measured end-to-end result improves.
children.subject: Thread-level parallelism for the independent output loop

children.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, investigate a per-thread SIMD kernel for the Black–Scholes and CND computation, suitable for later use inside a threaded loop but without adding OpenMP scheduling in this tree. Contrast compiler-vectorized scalar expressions where supported with explicit lane-wise math where useful; do not assume vector transcendental calls are available. Preserve the public input domain and tolerance, and use a correct fallback if needed. Inputs are only guaranteed 64-byte alignment at the start of input1, so handle per-array offsets, output alignment, and arbitrary n tails safely. Write all outputs, avoid test-value specialization, and compare correctness and wall time at both supplied sizes and budgets. Coordinate mentally with T3 by focusing on lane-level evaluation rather than repeating its scalar Horner experiment.
children.subject: SIMD math for the Black–Scholes and CND calculations

children.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, explore scalar-only arithmetic simplifications, especially evaluating the existing CND polynomial in Horner form and sharing repeated intermediates where valid. Do not add OpenMP or hand-coded SIMD, change the underlying option calculation, or assume tested input values. Verify the fixed tolerance for all valid inputs and compare wall time at both supplied sizes and thread budgets; record unsuccessful variants as well as any improvements.
children.subject: Scalar arithmetic and CND polynomial simplification
